description: We are a group of enthusiastic students excited to experience our first NASA Space Apps Challenge! We may be beginners, but we are curious, motivated and eager to learn. We welcome like-minded people interested in programming, data analysis, research, design, Earth science or technology. Prior experience isn't necessary—creativity, teamwork and a willingness to explore are what matter. Let's learn, collaborate and create something meaningful together! 🌍🚀
summary: FOREST WATCH is a proposed environmental monitoring platform that aims to explore deforestation and changes in forest cover using NASA satellite data. The project intends to make Earth observation data easier to understand by allowing users to select geographical regions, compare satellite observations from different years and visualise possible changes in forest cover through maps and graphs.Initially, we plan to focus on a selected forest region in Kerala, such as Wayanad. Using NASA resources such as Landsat and MODIS, we aim to investigate historical forest-cover changes and vegetation trends. The proposed platform will use Python for data analysis, Flask for backend development, and HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the user interface.FOREST WATCH aims to promote environmental awareness, make satellite information accessible to students and the public, and encourage forest conservation. During development, we will consider data accuracy, geographical coverage, seasonal variations and the difference between forest-cover loss and changes in vegetation greenness.The project is currently at the proposal stage. Our next goal is to access real NASA datasets, conduct comparisons and develop a basic working prototype.
details: FOREST WATCH is a proposed satellite-data-based environmental monitoring platform designed to help users explore deforestation and changes in forest cover over time. The project aims to make Earth observation data easier to understand through maps, visual comparisons and simple graphical representations.The proposed platform will allow users to select a geographical region, such as Wayanad, Kerala, and explore satellite observations from different years. By comparing these observations, users will be able to investigate possible changes in forest cover and vegetation. The planned system will also aim to present change trends through graphs and summaries.The project intends to improve environmental awareness, make satellite information more accessible to students and the public, and encourage further investigation into forest conservation.Our proposed technologies include Python for data processing and analysis, Flask for the backend, HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the user interface, and tools such as Folium and Chart.js for maps and visualisations. We plan to explore NASA Earth observation resources, particularly Landsat and MODIS datasets.The creative aspect of FOREST WATCH is its approach of turning complex satellite observations into an accessible and interactive forest-monitoring concept. Users will be able to explore a selected region and compare observations across different time periods.During development, our team will consider data accuracy, satellite resolution, geographical coverage, seasonal variations, statistical reliability and ease of use. We will also distinguish actual forest-cover changes from variations in vegetation greenness to avoid misleading conclusions.FOREST WATCH is currently at the proposal stage. The features and analysis described above are planned for future development and testing using actual satellite data.
